sets.relationshipLabel: a kind of landform and one named instance of it
sets.explanation: A gorge is a landform category and the Grand Canyon its most famous example, just as a waterfall names a category and Niagara names one of its most famous instances.

sets.relationshipLabel: an action and the action that answers or undoes it
sets.explanation: Erosion is answered by deposition, and a flood is answered by its recession — each pair names a process and the opposite process that reverses it.

sets.relationshipLabel: a river feature converts into what it eventually becomes
sets.explanation: Alluvium deposited over time builds a floodplain, just as a meander cut off from its river becomes an oxbow lake — each pair traces a feature into its later form.

sets.relationshipLabel: a visible sign and what it necessarily signals
sets.explanation: White water is the visible proof of rapids beneath it, and a high-water mark is the visible proof that a deluge once passed through — each sign necessarily points to its cause.

glossary.definition: loose soil, sand, and silt left behind by moving water
